title: Fastpath tool-gesture SDK proposal (WIP)
content:
Goal:
Provide an SDK-first surface and streaming contract that enables low-latency "fastpath" responses while supporting progressive tool-calls and structured partial output. The focus is on ergonomic client integration for mobile and web SDKs where latency and bandwidth are constrained, but correctness of tool-handshake and structured JSON output must be preserved.

Background / motivation:
- Users want predictable, very-low-latency fragments for interactive UIs (e.g., instant previews, autocompletes) while later tokens may contain structured results or tool invocations.
- Existing streaming patterns either: (a) block until parser-complete structured JSON is ready = high latency, or (b) stream unconstrained text fragments = poor developer ergonomics for tool-maps and replays.
- Need a middle ground: deliver small "gesture" fragments fast, with explicit metadata to let SDKs render partial UI and replay/complete tool calls deterministically.

Key ideas (fastpath tool-gesture):
1) Gesture frames: minimal, annotated delta frames intended for immediate render. Each frame contains: frame_id, seq_no, kind=(preview|gesture|schema-hint|final), payload (text or compact JSON fragment), and optional stable_cursor token. Gesture frames are not final; they are cheap to produce and safe to drop.

2) Structured-progress messages: when content requires structured output (e.g., JSON result or tool call), the runtime emits an initial schema-hint frame that describes the expected shape (names, types, optional tool endpoints) and later emits full structured frames or a finalization envelope. This avoids large single-block waits.

3) Tool-call handshake-by-gesture: tool invocation is represented as a 2-phase pair in-stream: a tool-intent gesture (fast) followed by tool-confirm (final). The SDK may choose to speculatively call a local shim or show a confirmation UI while the confirm arrives. If confirm never arrives, SDK must reconcile with final envelope.

4) SDK ergonomics: provide high-level primitives — onFragment(fragment) (fast), onSchemaHint(hint), onToolIntent(intent), onToolConfirm(confirm), onFinal(mutators) — plus a small local deterministic reconstructor that can merge fragments into a stable tree so apps can progressively display results and then commit.

5) Telemetry and SLOs: each frame carries a small telemetry header (server-latency-ms, queue-id, model-shard) enabling per-frame SLOs and billing attribution.

High-level API sketch (REST + streaming SSE/WebSocket):
- Client opens a session with session_id. Server returns initial session-state and prewarm hints.
- Streaming frames are delivered as compact JSONL lines (frame envelope). Minimal guaranteed ordering per seq_no per session.
- Important: frames with kind=gesture may be emitted out-of-band for speed but must include seq_no. Final frames (kind=final) are strictly ordered and idempotent.

Example fragment (human-readable):
{ frame_id: "f-23", seq_no: 23, kind: "gesture", payload: "Adding '—' to the summary...", stable_cursor: "c_0a9" }
Then later:
{ frame_id: "f-24", seq_no: 24, kind: "schema-hint", payload: { "result": { "type": "object", "fields": ["title","items[]"] }, "tools": ["search-v1","run-query"] } }
Finally:
{ frame_id: "f-40", seq_no: 40, kind: "final", payload: { "result": { "title": "Top three", "items": [{...}] }, "tool_calls": [{"id":"t-1","status":"ok","outputs":{}}] } }

SDK surface and ergonomic patterns:
- Low-level: stream.subscribe(sessionId, opts) -> yields frame events. SDK exposes a small transform utility: assembleFragments(frames[]) -> provisionalDocument.
- High-level: ProgressiveRenderer class that applies gestures to the DOM (or React state) with configurable fidelity lanes (fast/medium/final) and per-lane rendering hooks.
- Tool API: when onToolIntent arrives, SDK exposes pseudo-call runLocalShim(intent) that can return cached/simulated responses; it must be tagged as speculative and reconciled on onToolConfirm.
- Backpressure: client can send preferred-latency budget per session; server will adapt frame sizes and prefetch behavior.

Compatibility & fallbacks:
- Non-streaming clients receive final envelope only (server composes final).
- Clients that cannot handle partial structured frames can opt-in to a conservative mode where schema-hints are omitted, but the server must then increase finalization SLO and reduce gestures.

Observability / Debugging guidance:
- Frames should include trace_id, frame_latency_ms, and model_variant. SDK exposes a debug flag to keep raw frames in-memory for replay and a debug endpoint to push selected sessions to the debugging console.
- Provide unit tests for reconstruction logic with adversarial frame drops and reordering.

Security / Safety considerations:
- Tool-intent gestures must not contain secrets or PII. Confirm frames containing any external call outputs are subject to the same data classification rules as hosted tool outputs.
- Allow policy to mark certain tool intents as "deferred" (no speculative local runs).

Rollout plan (phased):
- Phase 0: Internal SDK + infra experiment (canary) with 10% of developer sandbox traffic. Implement server-side frame emitter and basic SDK reconstructor.
- Phase 1: Public beta for web SDKs (React) with opt-in flag. Collect telemetry on frame latency and tool-confirm delta.
- Phase 2: Mobile SDKs + conservative defaults. Add server-side optimization: gesture precomputation (cheap LM pass).
- Phase 3: Gradual enable for customers with latency SLAs; expose policy controls in Console (fidelity lanes, speculative-mode).

Operational requirements & infra notes:
- Serving runtime: need fast cheap-pass LM variant that can produce gestures without triggering heavy KV-cache misses. Suggest a low-cost 8-bit quantized microvariant tuned for short-prefix passes.
- Streaming channel: ensure per-session per-connection ordering guarantees for final frames. Gesture frames may be best-effort but should usually be ordered.
- Storage: ephemeral frame buffers retained for X hours for replay/debugging (configurable).

Open questions / tradeoffs (short):
- How to bound the size/complexity of schema-hint to avoid leaking model internals while still being useful?
- How often should a tool-intent be retried or hedged across model variants to guarantee confirm arrives?
- Billing model: do we charge per-frame tokens or only on final tokens? Hybrid? Need finance ops input.
- Client adoption friction: how much plumbing do we provide? (we prefer to provide higher-level renderer to maximize correct usage).

Next steps / action items:
- Engineering: spike on cheap-pass microvariant + server frame emitter (RW-ENG-1062). Owner: Marcus Li. ETA: 3 weeks.
- SDK: implement ProgressiveRenderer prototype in hosted-sdk repo (PR referenced above). Owner: Ava Chen. ETA: 2 weeks.
- Product: define Console toggles and customer-facing docs. Owner: Sofia Patel. ETA: 4 weeks.
- Legal/security: review tool-intent dataflow for regulated customers. Owner: Diego Ramirez. ETA: 2 weeks.

Notes to self / rough TODOs:
- Add a compact TLV format for frames (binary) for mobile; fallback to JSONL for debug.
- Draft sample migration guide for teams using synchronous structured responses.
- Prepare A/B test matrix (latency vs quality vs cost).

References and context links:
- Confluence: FASTPATH-STREAM-HANDOFF (linked_artifacts above)
- Jira: RW-2148 (experiment infra + telemetry)
- Github: hosted-sdk PR 682 (ProgressiveRenderer prototype)

If this direction looks good I will open a formal PRD (longer form) and schedule a cross-functional review with Eng infra, Serving, SDK, Security and GTM.

-- Sofia
